# Remember a display preference

Keep a choice the user makes about how things are shown (a list's order
or view, a collapsed panel, a default tab) with their account, so it is
the same in every browser and on every device: the auth pack's
preferences. A list's page, search, filters and sort go in the address
instead (recipe "Add a paginated, filterable list"); an open menu or a
draft stays in the component; a role, a permission, a token or a
confirmation is never a preference.

1. The routes. An app on `auth.Mount` has them: `api.authPreferences()`
   reads the account's document (`{subject, values}`) and
   `api.authPatchPreferences({ values })` changes the keys it names and
   keeps the others (a `null` removes one). An app with its own sign-in
   routes mounts the pack's methods behind `auth.Require()`: two handlers
   over `auth.From(ctx).Preferences(ctx)` and `PatchPreferences(ctx,
   req.Body)`, taking and returning the pack's types (`lidza snippet
   preference-handlers`).
2. Name keys by area, `<area>.<choice>` (`posts.view`, `posts.order`);
   values are any JSON. At most 128 keys, 4 KB a value, 32 KB the
   document: the server refuses more with a 422, and a patch sent with
   another account's id with a 409.
3. In the page, `usePreferences` from `src/preferences.ts` (an app
   created before it existed takes it with `lidza snippet preferences >
   src/preferences.ts`):

   ```tsx
   const prefs = usePreferences(
     { read: api.authPreferences, write: api.authPatchPreferences },
     session.userId,
     { 'posts.view': 'list' as 'list' | 'grid' },
     { accept: (_, value) => value === 'list' || value === 'grid' },
   )
   ```

   `prefs.values` are the defaults under the stored choices;
   `prefs.set({ 'posts.view': 'grid' })` shows the change at once and
   sends it (in order behind the one before; rolled back and reported in
   `prefs.error` when refused); `prefs.reset('posts.view')` removes it. A
   stored value of another type than the default, or one `accept`
   refuses, reads as the default, so an old shape never breaks the page.
   Before sign-out, `await prefs.flush()`, so the last change is stored.
   Pass the user's id from the session: the document is cached per
   account and every patch names it, so a slow write after a sign-in
   change is refused, not applied to the next user.
4. Test it in Go: patch a key, read it back, send `null` and see it
   gone, send another account's id and expect 409 (`lidza snippet
   handler-test` for the shape). In the browser (`e2e/`): make the
   choice, reload, it holds.
